Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. The Pakistani openers are yet to come out as we see the Irish team all in place. Now they arrive. Saim Ayub and Mohammad Rizwan to open.
...THE CHASE...

Ireland will be disappointed. They look 15 if not 25 runs short on a flat pitch. They were on course though for a score above 200. The way Andy Balbirnie and Lorcan Tucker were playing, it looked like Ireland will achieve their desired target but the wicket of skipper tilted things around in favour of the tourist who then didn't allow the home team to skyrocket any big overs in the fag end. Ireland still have enough runs on the board but they'll have to bowl exceptionally well to get a result.

A brilliant bowling performance by Pakistan and they'll be the happier team at the break. Pakistan opted to bowl first and it was a decent bowling performance until the halfway mark. They were conceding at 10 runs per over but we feel Imad Wasim's spell changed the course of the game. He took the big wicket of Lorcan Tucker who was smashing all around and since then it was hard for Ireland to slog in the main overs. The final 6-7 overs were just brilliant from Pakistan. Shaheen Afridi though was the pick as he finished with three wickets.

Babar Azam says they'll bowl first. Mentions the wicket was under covers, there could be a bit of moisture underneath. Shares they need strong performance, they have a plan and hopes they execute well. Informs Naseem Shah is not playing, Hasan Ali comes in place of him.
IRELAND (Playing XI) - Ross Adair, Andy Balbirnie, Lorcan Tucker (C/WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Neil Rock, Mark Adair, Graham Hume, Craig Young, Ben White.
PAKISTAN (Playing XI) - Babar Azam (C), Saim Ayub, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Fakhar Zaman, Azam Khan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Imad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Hasan Ali, Abbas Afridi, Mohammad Amir.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and will BOWL.

Hello and welcome to the third and final T20I between Ireland and Pakistan. After pulsating two games, it is time for the teams to fight for the ultimate game and clinch the series. Pakistan came into this game as the favourites but fumbled upon on a flat track as they lost the opener shockingly. However, unsurprisingly, they did come back strong to chase down a total close to 200 with ease. Ireland as a home team knows the conditions well and are expected to go head-to-head in the final game. Interestingly, the chasing team has won both games so that makes the toss even more crucial. Who are you supporting?
...MATCH DAY...

In the crucial decider of this 3-match T20 series between Ireland and Pakistan, it's all square at 1-1. Ireland owned the first game, but Pakistan came back strong and snagged the second one. Both matches have seen some big scores, and interestingly, the team batting second has emerged victorious both times. Despite Pakistan's strong performance in the second game, Ireland put up a commendable fight, showcasing great character as various players stepped up to contribute to the home team. From Andy Balbirnie's determined innings in the opener to Lorcan Tucker's stellar fifty in the second match, the Irish batters have displayed grit and determination. With crucial cameos down the order from players like Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, and Gareth Delany, the Irish team has managed to strike a good balance. The skipper, Paul Stirling, will be keen to make his mark and contribute more with the bat after two disappointing outings. However, in the bowling department, there needs to be a lot of improvement. Despite setting a formidable total of 193 runs on the board, Ireland struggled to pick up timely wickets. Bowlers like Graham Hume, Mark Adair, Craig Young, and Ben White will need to step up their game to address this issue. On the flip side, while Pakistan displayed some signs of improvement, they still have areas to work on, particularly in the fielding department. Babar Azam came back strongly and notched up a brilliant half-century in the first game but had a disappointing outing as he walked out on a duck in the previous game. Although Mohammad Rizwan rescued Pakistan with a formidable 75 with Fakhar Zaman too, responsibly adding his valuable contribution with the bat that cruised Pakistan to the win. They possess a robust middle order, with Iftikhar Ahmed standing out for his ability to deliver clutch finishes and boost the scoring rate in the backend. Mohammad Amir was swapped in for Shadab Khan, didn't quite live up to expectations in the previous match, and would aim to be more economical. Shaheen Afridi too, has been a bit pricey in this series but has taken wickets to his name. Abbas Afridi has impressed with the ball and he leads the wicket-taking charts for the series thus far. With Ireland, fueled by the support of the home crowd, eager to shake up Pakistan and clinch the series, their victory would undoubtedly boost their drive for the upcoming T20 World Cup. Meanwhile, Pakistan aims to maintain the momentum from the second match, albeit with improvements in certain areas. It is surely going to be a humdinger of a series decider. Who do you think has an edge?
